source_text: Regula est autem fidei, ut iam hinc quid defendamus profiteamur, illa scilicet qua creditur unum omnino deum esse nec alium praeter mundi conditorem, qui universa de nihilo produxerit per verbum suum primo omnium demissum; id verbum filium eius appellatum, in nomine dei varie visum a patriarchis, in prophetis semper auditum, postremo delatum ex spiritu patris dei et virtute in virginem Mariam, carnem factum in utero eius et ex ea natum exisse Iesum Christum, exinde praedicasse novam legem et novam promissionem regni caelorum, virtutes fecisse, cruci fixum tertia die resurrexisse, in caelos ereptum sedisse ad dexteram patris, misisse vicariam vim spiritus sancti, qui credentes agat, venturum cum claritate ad sumendos sanctos in vitae aeternae et promissorum caelestium fructum et ad profanos iudicandos igni perpetuo, facta utriusque partis resuscitatione cum carnis restitutione. Haec regula a Christo, ut probabitur, instituta nullas habet apud nos quaestiones, nisi quas haereses inferunt et quae haereticos faciunt.
orientation: Tertullian opens his treatise by stating the rule of faith, the fixed summary of Christian belief, which he will defend against heretics.
pass_a_gloss: The rule [is] moreover of faith, so that from now [on] what we defend we may profess, that [rule] namely by which it is believed [that] one altogether God [is] and not another besides the creator of the world, who all things from nothing produced through his word first of all sent down; this word [was] called his son, in the name of God variously seen by the patriarchs, in the prophets always heard, at last brought down from the spirit of the father God and power into the virgin Mary, made flesh in her womb and from her born [and] went out [as] Jesus Christ, from then [on] preached [the] new law and [the] new promise of the kingdom of the heavens, powers did, fixed to the cross [on] the third day rose again, into the heavens taken up sat at the right hand of the father, sent [the] vicarious force of the holy spirit, who the believers may lead, [and] to come with glory to take up the saints into the fruit of eternal life and of the heavenly promises and to judge the profane with perpetual fire, [with] the resurrection of both parts having been made with the restoration of the flesh. This rule by Christ, as will be proved, instituted has no questions among us, except those which heresies bring in and which make heretics.

choices.why: omnino intensifies the oneness; 'altogether' preserves the force of total singularity
conditor is the standard term for the creator; 'creator' is the fixed rendering

choices.term: per verbum suum primo omnium demissum
choices.english: through his word first of all sent down
choices.why: primo omnium means 'first of all things'; the word was sent down before all else
rejected: through his word sent down before all
through his word first sent down

choices.english: vicarious force of the holy spirit
choices.why: vicariam means acting in place of Christ; 'vicarious' preserves the legal sense of substitution

choices.term: ad sumendos sanctos in vitae aeternae et promissorum caelestium fructum
choices.english: to take up the saints into the fruit of eternal life and of the heavenly promises
choices.why: fructum is singular and governs both genitives; 'fruit' preserves the metaphor of enjoyment
rejected: to receive the saints into the enjoyment of eternal life
to take the saints for the fruit

choices.term: facta utriusque partis resuscitatione cum carnis restitutione
choices.english: [with] the resurrection of both parts having been made with the restoration of the flesh
choices.why: utriusque partis means both groups (saints and profane); the ablative absolute is preserved
rejected: after both parties have been raised
when the resurrection of both sides has happened

pass_b_english: The rule of faith—so that from this point I declare what we defend—is that by which we believe there is one God alone, and no other besides the creator of the world, who produced all things from nothing through his word sent down first of all. This word, called his Son, was seen in the name of God in various ways by the patriarchs, was always heard in the prophets, and was finally brought down by the Spirit and power of God the Father into the virgin Mary, became flesh in her womb, and was born from her as Jesus Christ. From then on he preached the new law and the new promise of the kingdom of heaven, performed miracles, was crucified, rose on the third day, was taken up into heaven, and sat down at the right hand of the Father. He sent the vicarious power of the Holy Spirit to lead believers, and he will come with glory to take up the saints into the fruit of eternal life and the heavenly promises, and to judge the profane with perpetual fire, after the resurrection of both groups has taken place with the restoration of the flesh. This rule, instituted by Christ, as will be proved, has no questions among us except those which heresies introduce and which make heretics.
